name: Castillo San Felipe del Morro
verse: Six decks of stone stare at the waves that once carried galleons and pirates. Its cannons spoke, its walls held, and the salt wind still circles them, beyond the western ocean.

name: Castillo San Felipe de Barajas
verse: A hill of tunnels and walls built to keep the treasure fleets safe from raiders off the sea. No army ever took it, beyond the western ocean.

name: Abu Simbel
verse: Four seated giants carved from the cliff face the sunrise; twice a year the light walks deep inside to touch the gods. Sand on every side, where the first people walked.

name: Iguazu Falls
verse: A throat of thunder in the green; no hand carved these cliffs, and the mist never settles over the leaves, beyond the western ocean.

name: Sankore Mosque
verse: Walls of mud and palm wood where scholars prayed and copied books while the dunes crept closer every year, where the first people walked.

name: Christ the Redeemer
verse: Arms open on a peak above the clouds, built to be seen by a whole city below, beyond the western ocean.

name: Old Fort of Zanzibar
verse: Coral-stone walls by a spice harbour where dhows rock on the tide; it was built to keep the sea's raiders out, where the first people walked.

name: Karnak
verse: A forest of stone columns where priests sang to the gods beside the great river that floods and gives life, where the first people walked.

name: Taj Mahal
verse: White marble that glows pink at dawn on a river's bank, raised by an emperor so his beloved could sleep forever, where the silk roads ran.

name: Fasil Ghebbi
verse: Castles of kings high in the cool mountains, towers and walls where emperors kept their courts, where the first people walked.

name: Sydney Opera House
verse: White sails that never leave the harbour, built to be seen from every boat on the water, at the bottom of the world.

name: Edinburgh Castle
verse: A castle on an old volcano above crowded streets and smoking chimneys; its walls held off siege after siege, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Grand Canyon
verse: A river cut this wound in the red earth over a million years; no hand shaped it, and the dry wind sings in it, beyond the western ocean.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda
verse: A golden spire above a busy city, where monks pray and bells ring around relics older than kings, where the silk roads ran.

name: Victoria Falls
verse: The smoke that thunders: a great river falls into a crack in the earth that no hand made, where the first people walked.

name: Statue of Liberty
verse: A copper giant with a torch greets ships from the sea, built to be the first thing the tired travellers saw, beyond the western ocean.

name: Colosseum
verse: A broken ring of arches in the heart of a crowded city, raised to be seen and to hold fifty thousand roaring voices, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Ahu Tongariki
verse: Fifteen stone faces stand with their backs to the sea, carved to watch over their people, on an island at the bottom of the world.

name: Sagrada Familia
verse: Towers like melting candles rise from a crowded city; a house of prayer still unfinished after a hundred years, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Walls of Dubrovnik
verse: Pale walls wrap a city on the sea; no fleet broke them in centuries, and the salt wind walks their towers, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Eiffel Tower
verse: An iron lady over a crowded city, built for a fair and meant to be seen from every street, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Alhambra
verse: A red palace-fortress on a hill beneath snowy peaks; sultans held it behind their walls until the very last, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Table Mountain
verse: A flat-topped peak where a tablecloth of cloud spreads at noon; no hand levelled it, where the first people walked.

name: Uluru
verse: A red rock alone in the red sand, glowing at sunset; no hand shaped it, at the bottom of the world.

name: Teotihuacan
verse: An avenue of the dead runs between pyramids on a wide plain; the people who built this city vanished before anyone wrote their name, beyond the western ocean.

name: Acropolis
verse: Marble columns on a rock above a crowded city, where the goddess of wisdom was worshipped, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Tulum
verse: A walled city on a cliff above turquoise waves; its people left long ago and only iguanas walk its streets, beyond the western ocean.

name: Ait Benhaddou
verse: A fortified village of earth towers on the caravan road, its walls guarding traders from the desert raiders, where the first people walked.

name: Pyramids of Giza
verse: Three mountains of stone at the edge of the sand, raised so that kings might sleep forever and never be forgotten, where the first people walked.

name: Goreme
verse: Chimneys of soft rock rise from high valleys where balloons drift at dawn; wind and rain carved them, no hand, where the silk roads ran.

name: Hagia Sophia
verse: A great dome floats over a crowded city between two seas; church, then mosque, a house of prayer for fifteen hundred years, among the old kingdoms of the north.

name: Borobudur
verse: A stone mountain of shrines rises from green jungle; pilgrims climb its terraces past hundreds of quiet Buddhas, where the silk roads ran.
